end.summary:
Reyansh practised identifying top, front, and side views of cars, cones, cups, caps, and cylinders.
They stated that a front view shows what is visible from the front and a top view shows what is visible from above.
They correctly described a cone’s top view as a circle and side view as a triangle, and a cylinder’s side view as a rectangle.
They matched 0 of 2 object-view items without help; teach-back was not passed.
They drew known object features even when those features would be hidden from the stated viewpoint; this was not corrected later.
end.parentNote: Reyansh practised drawing and identifying solid shapes from the top, front, and side. Using a car and a helicopter view helped them explain that a view shows only what can be seen from that position, and they correctly used the pointy-versus-flat top method for cones and cylinders. They mixed up whether a hidden feature, such as a cup handle, should be included, and this was not corrected later in the lesson. At home, ask them to look at a toy from one marked position and draw only the parts visible from there.
